title: TypeScript Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced TypeScript reference covering strict configuration, inference, narrowing, generics, object modeling, classes, modules, async code, runtime validation, advanced types, declaration files, and scalable builds.

sections.title: Configuration, Values & Inference
sections.description: Start strict, preserve useful literal information, and let inference work locally while documenting public boundaries.

subtopics.title: Strict tsconfig Foundations
subtopics.description: Use strict checking and choose module settings that match the real runtime and bundler. TypeScript 6 enables stricter modern defaults for newly initialized projects.

callouts.title: Match the Runtime
callouts.text: module, moduleResolution, target, and lib describe the environment. A configuration that type-checks but does not match Node, a browser bundler, or the emitted package can still fail at runtime.

subtopics.title: Inference, Annotations & Literal Types
subtopics.description: Allow inference for obvious local values; annotate public inputs, recursive functions, and boundaries where the intended contract matters.

callouts.title: as const Is Deeply Readonly in the Type
callouts.text: A const assertion preserves literal values and marks object/array members readonly in the inferred type. It does not freeze the value at runtime.

subtopics.title: Validate Shape with satisfies
subtopics.description: satisfies checks compatibility without replacing the expression's more specific inferred type.

callouts.title: Prefer satisfies to Broad Annotation
callouts.text: Use a type annotation when you want the variable to have that declared type. Use satisfies when you want validation while retaining precise property types.

sections.title: Unions, Narrowing & Exhaustiveness
sections.description: Model alternatives explicitly and narrow them with evidence available at runtime.

subtopics.title: unknown, any & never
subtopics.description: unknown requires proof before use, any opts out of checking, and never represents an impossible value or non-returning path.

subtopics.title: Discriminated Unions
subtopics.description: Give each variant a stable literal discriminator so control-flow analysis can narrow safely.

callouts.title: Avoid Boolean Flag Combinations
callouts.text: A discriminated union makes invalid state combinations unrepresentable and gives rendering, reducers, and protocol handlers exhaustive branches.

subtopics.title: Type Guards, Assertion Functions & Exhaustiveness
subtopics.description: A predicate returns boolean evidence; an assertion function throws when evidence is absent. Both must perform real runtime checks.

callouts.title: Interfaces Do Not Exist at Runtime
callouts.text: Do not use instanceof with an interface or assume parsed JSON has a class prototype. Check structure explicitly or validate with a runtime schema library.

sections.title: Generics & Type Composition
sections.description: Use generics to preserve relationships between inputs and outputs, not merely to replace specific types with placeholders.

subtopics.title: Generic Functions & Constraints
subtopics.description: Constrain only the capability an implementation needs and let callers retain their more specific types.

callouts.title: Do Not Add Unused Type Parameters
callouts.text: A type parameter should relate two or more positions or preserve caller information. Otherwise, use a concrete type or unknown.

subtopics.title: Mapped Types & Utility Types
subtopics.description: Mapped types transform property sets; standard utilities cover common selection, omission, optionality, and immutability operations.

callouts.title: Readonly Is Shallow
callouts.text: Readonly<T> prevents assignment to top-level properties in the type system. Nested objects remain mutable unless modeled recursively, and no runtime freeze is applied.

subtopics.title: Conditional, infer & Template Literal Types
subtopics.description: Conditional types select types based on assignability; infer captures a component; template literal types model constrained string protocols.

callouts.title: Keep Type Computation Readable
callouts.text: Complex conditional types can slow checking and produce unreadable errors. Name intermediate concepts and prefer ordinary interfaces when metaprogramming does not improve the public API.

sections.title: Objects, Classes & Modules
sections.description: Model stable boundaries structurally and distinguish compile-time visibility from JavaScript runtime behavior.

subtopics.title: Interfaces, Type Aliases & Structural Typing
subtopics.description: Interfaces excel at extendable object contracts; aliases name unions, primitives, tuples, functions, and computed types.

callouts.title: Structural Compatibility Can Admit Extra Capabilities
callouts.text: Compatibility is based on members, not declared names. Use branded types when two primitive values must not be interchangeable despite identical representation.

subtopics.title: Classes, Parameter Properties & Runtime Privacy
subtopics.description: Class modifiers mostly guide the checker. JavaScript #private fields provide runtime-enforced privacy.

subtopics.title: ES Modules, Type-Only Imports & Package Exports
subtopics.description: Use import type for erased dependencies and publish declarations that match the package's real ESM/CommonJS entry points.

callouts.title: Use Runtime File Specifiers
callouts.text: Under Node ESM modes, relative imports commonly use the emitted .js extension in TypeScript source. Do not rely on the checker to invent a runtime resolution strategy.

sections.title: Async Code & Runtime Boundaries
sections.description: Types disappear after compilation, so network, storage, environment, and user input still need runtime validation.

subtopics.title: Promises, Awaited Values & Cancellation
subtopics.description: An async function always returns Promise<T>. Model failures deliberately and propagate AbortSignal through cancellable operations.

callouts.title: Promise Rejection Is Not in the Return Type
callouts.text: Promise<User> describes fulfillment. JavaScript permits any rejection value, so catch unknown and normalize errors at process, transport, or UI boundaries.

subtopics.title: Validate Untrusted Data
subtopics.description: Treat JSON.parse, fetch bodies, environment variables, storage, and postMessage payloads as unknown until checked.

callouts.title: Assertions Do Not Validate
callouts.text: value as User only instructs the compiler. It neither checks nor converts the runtime value and can move a boundary error deeper into the application.

subtopics.title: Domain Errors & Result Types
subtopics.description: Use thrown errors for exceptional control flow or a discriminated result when failure is an expected value callers must handle.

sections.title: Declarations, Project Scale & Migration
sections.description: Keep public types small, build packages in dependency order, and treat compiler upgrades as reviewed migrations.

subtopics.title: Declaration Files & Library Design
subtopics.description: .d.ts files describe JavaScript APIs without implementing them. Export only supported contracts and test declarations from a consumer perspective.

callouts.title: Avoid Global Augmentation
callouts.text: Prefer module exports. Global declarations and module augmentation are appropriate only when the runtime truly mutates that shared namespace or third-party module.

subtopics.title: Project References & Incremental Builds
subtopics.description: Composite projects create explicit dependency boundaries for large repositories and allow tsc --build to order and cache work.

subtopics.title: TypeScript 6.0 Migration Checklist
subtopics.description: TypeScript 6 is the compatibility bridge toward the native TypeScript 7 toolchain and removes or changes long-deprecated configuration behavior.

npx tsc --version
npx tsc --noEmit --extendedDiagnostics
npx tsc --showConfig

callouts.title: Review New Defaults Explicitly
callouts.text: New TypeScript 6 projects receive modern strict defaults. Existing projects should compare --showConfig output, remove deprecated options, check module resolution, and run the complete test/build matrix before upgrading.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Enable strict checking, avoid any leakage, validate runtime inputs, model variants with discriminated unions, use type-only imports, test declarations, measure checker performance, and pin a supported compiler version in CI.
